newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Hunters militia attack town in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Hunters militia attack town in Sierra Leone.

text.p: Kamajor traditional hunters attacked soldiers loyal to Sierra Leone's military ruler Johnny Paul Koroma in the eastern region capital of Kenema on Thursday, residents and the governor of the region said.
Captain Eddie Kanneh told Reuters by telephone from the town that truck loads of Kamajors, who have refused to rally to the May 25 coup, attacked the town on several fronts.
Residents fleeing the town reported many dead, including civilians. They said by telephone that the fighting began early on Thursday when most people were still in bed.

"There are so many bodies of Kamajors lying around killed in the battle today between government soldiers and Kamajors for control of Kenema," Kanneh said, adding that soldiers had suffered gunshot wounds and other injuries.

He said the army had driven back the Kamajor attackers and would not let them near the town again. Red Cross workers, contacted by telephone, said that fighting was continuing and that Kamajors were still in the town.
The attack was the latest in a series of clashes between the Kamajors and the army in the region.
Junior army officers seized power on May 25 toppling civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who took office in March 1996 after multi-party elections that ended four years of army rule.

Kabbah used the Kamajors as a civil militia to help the army push back rebels who took up arms in 1991. The coup leaders accuse him of humiliating the army and blocking peace with the rebels, who rallied to the coup and have flooded into the capital Freetown.
Koroma was sworn in as head of state on Tuesday and pledged to restore peace and eventually democracy to the war-weary West African nation.
"We will form a very broad-based government incorporating every sector of the community. We will make sure that every tribe is represented," he added.
Koroma said that both the rebel Revolutionary United Front and the Kamajor traditional hunters, who have kept their distance from the coup leaders, would be represented.
Kamajor leaders have said that they will not join a broad-based government and want to stay out of politics.
Civilian politicians and Sierra Leone's West African neighbours insist that Kabbah be reinstated, something the coup leaders have rejected.
Nigerian gunboats bombarded the capital Freetown in a show of force on June 2 and dissident soldiers and rebels attacked Nigerian soldiers who were there under a defence accord.
The United States, France, Lebanon and other nations evacuated their own and other foreign nationals.
A widely anticipated Nigerian attack has not materialised.
Military officials said on Monday they had arrested eight army officers and seven civilians on suspicion of plotting a fresh coup and trying to enlist the support of rebel fighters.
